We note that  $ \delta_{\varphi} $ in (22) is one possible flow bound. When more information about the closed-loop system may be leveraged (e.g., contraction, one-sided Lipschitzness [16], or linearity), this bound can be made tighter [17].

Having established the flow error bound in (21), we now introduce tightening terms that allow us to make constraints on the estimated backup flow sufficient for satisfying constraints on the true backup flow. These tightening terms are denoted as  $ \epsilon $ and  $ \epsilon_{b} $, and they are constructed such that

$$ \begin{align*}\epsilon(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)&\geq h(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\varphi}}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t))-h(\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x})),\\\epsilon_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x},t)&\geq h_{\mathrm{b}}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\varphi}}_{\mathrm{b}}(T,\boldsymbol{x},t))-h_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(T,\boldsymbol{x})),\end{align*} $$

hold for all  $ \tau \in [0, T] $,  $ \boldsymbol{x} \in \mathcal{X} $, and  $ t \geq 0 $, providing bounds on the effect of the parameter uncertainty on safety. For example, by the Lipschitz continuity of  $ h $ and  $ h_b $, we may define continuously differentiable tightening functions as

$$ \begin{align*}\epsilon(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)&\triangleq L_{h}\delta_{\varphi}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t),\\\epsilon_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x},t)&\triangleq L_{h_{\mathrm{b}}}\delta_{\varphi}(T,\boldsymbol{x},t),\end{align*} $$

where  $ L_{h} $ and  $ L_{h_{b}} $ are the Lipschitz constants of h and  $ h_{b} $. For convex or quadratic barriers, even tighter  $ \epsilon $ and  $ \epsilon_{b} $ terms may be obtained [18, Remark 2].

To enhance robustness against parameter estimation errors, similar to the uncertainty estimator-based bCBF method proposed in [17], we define a time-varying inner approximation  $ \widehat{C}_{\mathrm{I}}(t) $ of the true implicit safe set  $ C_{\mathrm{I}} $ in (6):

$$ \widehat{\mathcal{C}}_{\mathrm{I}}(t)\triangleq\left\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathcal{X}:\begin{array}{l}\bar{h}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)\geq0,\quad\forall\tau\in[0,T],\\ \bar{h}_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x},t)\geq0\end{array}\right\}, $$
for all  $ t \geq 0 $, where the tightening terms are incorporated in

$$ \begin{align*}\bar{h}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)&\triangleq h(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\varphi}}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t))-\epsilon(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t),\\\bar{h}_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x},t)&\triangleq h_{\mathrm{b}}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\varphi}}_{\mathrm{b}}(T,\boldsymbol{x},t))-\epsilon_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x},t).\end{align*} $$
We remark that, since  $ \epsilon, \epsilon_b \geq 0 $,  $ \widehat{C}_I(t) \subseteq C_I $.
Having constructed a known subset of  $ C_I $, we are now in a position to enforce the forward invariance of  $ \widehat{C_I}(t) $. We impose that the control input  $ u $ must satisfy

$$ \begin{align*}\dot{\bar{h}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t,\boldsymbol{u})&\geq-\alpha\big(\bar{h}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)\big),\quad\forall\tau\in[0,T],\\\dot{\bar{h}}_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x},t,\boldsymbol{u})&\geq-\alpha_{\mathrm{b}}\big(\bar{h}_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x},t)\big),\end{align*} $$
for all  $ x \in \widehat{C}_I(t) $ and  $ t \geq 0 $. By calculating the time derivatives via the chain rule, these inequalities can be written as

$$ \begin{align*}a(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{u},t)+\boldsymbol{c}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{u},t)^{\top}\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(t)&\geq0,\\a_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{u},t)+\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{u},t)^{\top}\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(t)&\geq0,\end{align*} $$

where the expressions of $a$, $a_{\mathrm{b}}$, $c$, and $c_{\mathrm{b}}$ are derived in the Appendix. Note that while the $a$, $a_{\mathrm{b}}$, $c$, and $c_{\mathrm{b}}$ coefficients are known, the parameter estimation error $\tilde{\theta}(t)$ is unknown, and hence (28) cannot be enforced directly.
Instead, we apply the robust adaptive bCBF conditions
$$ a(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{u},t)+\inf_{\boldsymbol{\eta}\in\widetilde{\Theta}(t)}\boldsymbol{c}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{u},t)^{\top}\boldsymbol{\eta}\geq0, $$
$$ a_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{u},t)+\inf_{\boldsymbol{\eta}\in\widetilde{\Theta}(t)}\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{u},t)^{\top}\boldsymbol{\eta}\geq0. $$

These inequalities enforce the bCBF conditions for all admissible parameter estimation errors inside the known error set  $ \widetilde{\Theta}(t) $ given by (14). The inner minimizations are linear programs (LPs) over the component-wise estimation error set. Theorem 1. Consider the uncertain system (10), an estimator in Definition 1, the safe set  $ \mathcal{C}_S $ in (2), the backup controller  $ \mathbf{k}_b $, the backup set  $ \mathcal{C}_B $ in (5), and the time-varying set  $ \widehat{\mathcal{C}}_I(t) $ in (25). Suppose Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. Then, any locally Lipschitz controller satisfying (31)–(34) for all  $ \tau \in [0, T] $ renders  $ \widehat{\mathcal{C}}_I(t) $ forward invariant for (10). Consequently, every closed-loop trajectory starting in  $ \widehat{\mathcal{C}}_I(0) $ remains in  $ \mathcal{C}_S\colon \mathbf{x}(0) \in \widehat{\mathcal{C}}_I(0) \implies \mathbf{x}(t) \in \mathcal{C}_S, \forall t \geq 0 $.

Proof. By strong duality, the dual inequality and equality conditions in (31)–(34) imply the primal robust inequalities (29) and (30). Since  $ \hat{\theta}(t) \in \tilde{\Theta}(t) $, these primal inequalities imply (27). Consequently, the comparison lemma gives the forward invariance of  $ \hat{C}_1(t) $. From the tightening construction (23), we have  $ \hat{C}_1(t) \subseteq C_1 $. Since  $ \tau = 0 $ is included in the definition of  $ C_1 $, we also have  $ \hat{C}_1 \subseteq C_S $. Therefore, every closed-loop trajectory starting in  $ \hat{C}_1(0) $ remains in  $ C_S $.

Having established the robust safety constraints in (31)–(34), we now introduce an optimization problem, in the form of a QP, that enables the synthesis of safe controllers. Let the backup horizon be discretized by  $ \tau_j = jT/N_T $ for  $ j \in \{0, \ldots, N_T\} $, and define the decision variable vector as  $ w^{\triangle}(u, \{\mu_{\tau_j}\}_{j=0}^N, \mu_b) $ that contains  $ N_w^{\triangle} = m + (N_T + 2)2N $ elements. With  $ w $, we formulate an adaptive safety filter that minimally modifies a potentially unsafe primary controller  $ k_p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{U} $ into a safe controller:

$$ \begin{aligned}\boldsymbol{k}^{*}(t,\boldsymbol{x},\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}})=&\underset{w\in\mathbb{R}^{N_{w}}}{\arg\min}\quad\|\boldsymbol{u}-\boldsymbol{k}_{\mathrm{p}}(\boldsymbol{x})\|^{2}\quad(35)\\&\text{s.t.}\quad\boldsymbol{u}\in\mathcal{U},(33),(34),\\&\quad(31),(32)\text{at}\tau_{j},j\in\{0,\ldots,N_{T}\}.\end{aligned} $$

Note that (35) is a QP, since its constraints are affine in w.

Remark 1. Theorem 1 uses continuous time safety conditions over  $ \tau \in [0, T] $, while the QP in (35) enforces discretized constraints on a grid using  $ \tau_j $. As in standard bCBF implementations, one can add inter-sample margins or choose a sufficiently fine grid to account for the discretization error.

Remark 2. The proposed method with the QP in (35) ensures safety without requiring the notoriously restrictive persistent excitation (PE) condition on the regression matrix. Furthermore, as the certified bounds  $ \rho_i(t) $ decrease, the flow error bound  $ \delta_\varphi $ and the tightening terms  $ \epsilon $,  $ \epsilon_\mathrm{b} $ shrink; therefore, the inner approximation  $ \widehat{C}_I(t) $ approaches  $ C_I $ as  $ \rho_i(t) \to 0 $.
